nearest_prior_results: Bergé, Limouzy and Schivre, Output-linear time enumeration of potential maximal cliques, arXiv:2610.19850v3 (20 October 2026), Theorem 1: O(n^4 m |PMC(G)|) total time; Section 1.4 leaves polynomial delay open. Lemmas 11/12 and Theorems 8–11/Corollary 3 supply the inherited seed/preimage structure. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19850v3

Kenig, Enumerating Small Potential Maximal Cliques with Fixed-Parameter Delay, arXiv:2610.24856v1 (17 October 2026), Theorem 1.1: 2^{O(k^3)} n^4 log n initial/inter-output/final delay for size-at-most-k constrained outputs; k=n is not polynomial. https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24856v1

Grigoriev, Kobayashi, Tamaki and van der Zanden, IPEC 2025 article 21, Theorem 32: polynomial delay on triconnected plane graphs; Proposition 29 already uses a separator-saturating triangulation and an extending maximal clique. substantive_delta: A full all-graph, all-size worst-case polynomial-delay enumerator. The generator emits witnessed bounded-fiber separator helper PMCs while consuming seeds, pauses recursive enumeration at injectively lifted emissions, and establishes both every output-rank time and complete termination with an additive polynomial recurrence. Empty/disconnected/complete inputs and final delay are explicitly covered; exponential storage is allowed.
why_nonroutine: This does not follow by feeding the known total-output-linear PMC algorithm into a generic buffer. A global separator/output count comparison gives no control on a long early separator prefix, and an output-rank induction alone does not pay for a child finalization tail. Actual helper emissions force prefix progress, while exact suspension and the simultaneous termination invariant prevent a multiplying recursive coefficient. These are algorithmic modifications and a new prefix-time argument resolving the stated general open guarantee; the known structural, extension, lift and buffering results themselves are explicitly credited.
significance: Polynomial delay for every graph and every PMC size gives a fixed polynomial time guarantee for any requested number of distinct outputs and all boundary waits, beyond the nearest total-time and restricted/parameterized-delay guarantees. This is substantive progress on a central graph-enumeration primitive. It establishes neither polynomial space nor improved total-time exponents for treewidth; its competitive STOC significance remains uncertain and is separately labelled working_paper.
